main_text.l: in ordine ad culpam : & verum est illud
Apostoli dictum etiam in hoc sensu, et-
{x}Lex justo non est posita. Intendit ergo
Lex primario, directe, per se, & [illegible, ~6 letters]
ad supplicium autem & poenam non ob-
officii aut contemptu aut neglectu. U-
videtur Apostolus, Rom. 13. ubi agit de
E quibus verbis tria colligo ad praesens
ci vinculo posse nos obligari ad idem
supplicii : hoc enim volunt illa, [?]διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν, & διὰ τὴν
ὀργήν. Alterum, priorem & potiorem apud omnes pios esse
plicii metum. Tertium, ex debito officii
ntiae. Unde etiam manifestum est, nos

page.notes: The Greek phrase "διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν, & διὰ τὴν ὀργήν" is copied with doubt on its first word; the Greek word after "&" in the first paragraph could not be read and is marked illegible. The "x" reference in the text (before "Lex justo") and the "x" note in the margin (1 Tim.1 9.) are both marked. The "y" reference and note (Rom. 13. 5.) are marked. The cut-off letters along the right edge belong to the neighbouring page and were left out. No catchword or signature is visible.
